about: How a count of votes or a sum of money is said aloud in talk: a close count exactly, a larger one as people round it, never the tally to the vote or the cent. Read by src/english/count-words.ts; the director passes the number.

exactVotesBelow.checkedAgainst: Below this many votes a close count is said exactly (a loss by 7 is 7); above it a count is said as people round it ("about 60"). Local counts in the sources run from a few dozen votes to a few hundred (Jefferson City 2013, 55; Raincross 2019, 222; docs/design/scenes/from-life/household-after-the-loss.md).

lateSteps.about: How long rent has gone unpaid, said as people say it in talk (the notice at home, Nov 8: a shortfall left for two months is 'about two months', never '61 days'). Each row: the days below which the phrase is said. Read by lateSaid in src/english/count-words.ts; the director passes the days.
lateSteps.source: Calendar months of 30.4 days (365 / 12), rounded to the nearest month; under a month said in weeks as people say them. The phrase is rounding in speech, not a measure the game decides on.

clock.about: A time of day and a span of work hours as people say them in talk ("I'm on at seven-thirty", "eight hours"): the hour in words on a twelve-hour clock, the minutes rounded to the quarter hour, noon and midnight by name. Words composer, talk on ordinary days (Nov 12).

stepMinutes.checkedAgainst: People give a shift's start to the quarter hour in speech ("seven-thirty", "a quarter to nine"); work slots in the work-spans engine start on the quarter hour or the hour.

term.about: A term of office in years as people say it in a speech ("four years"), from the term record's length: the number in words up to twelve. Words composer, an address's occasion (lead, Nov 13).

length.about: A prison term or other length of months as people say it in talk ("eight months", "three years"): whole years when the months make whole years, else months. Read by lengthSaid in src/english/count-words.ts.
